label: Мало
description: A 10-sentence usage card for мало (little; few; not much).

missions.fullAnalysis: Strategic focus: Scarcity with genitive. 'Мало' takes the genitive 'денег' to mean little money. The core pattern is 'мало' plus a genitive noun, expressing insufficient quantity.
Strategic focus: Modifying a verb. 'Мало' attaches to 'спит' to mean he sleeps little. With a verb it needs no genitive noun and measures the small extent of the action.
Strategic focus: Genitive of a mass noun. 'Мало' governs the genitive singular 'снега' to say there is little snow. Mass nouns take the genitive singular after this word.
Strategic focus: Few countable items. 'Мало' takes the genitive plural 'мест' to mean few places, with the adjective 'интересных' agreeing in that case. It marks a small number of countable things.
Strategic focus: Limited knowledge. 'Мало' modifies 'знаю' to mean I know little about it. Attached to the verb, it conveys a small degree without any genitive complement.
Strategic focus: Scarcity in the past. 'Мало времени' uses the genitive singular 'времени' for little time. The neuter past 'было' agrees with the quantity expression as a neuter subject.
Strategic focus: Verb modification of frequency. 'Мало' attaches to 'говорит' to mean he speaks little at meetings. It describes how seldom or briefly the action occurs.
Strategic focus: Few people present. 'Мало' takes the genitive plural 'учеников' to state that few pupils are present. The pattern 'мало' plus genitive plural fits countable nouns.
Strategic focus: Extent of an activity. 'Мало' modifies 'отдыхали' to mean we rested little this summer. Placed before the verb, it measures the small amount of rest taken.
Strategic focus: Standalone shortfall. 'Мало' works as a predicate meaning 'not enough', sharpened by 'слишком'. The genitive 'этого' points to the substance that falls short for everyone.
